currentState: Chapter 7 (Sylvanas's POV): the work splits for the first time on hostile ground and holds. Sylvanas sends Jaina out of sight with a stranger (Corin) and Lyriel ('Proudmoore. The sample room. Take him.') and goes into the district herself; Jaina names the limits of her half ('I'll know what's in the bags. I won't know who put it there.'), Sylvanas takes the other ('That's mine.'). They meet again at the post and the two halves fit at once: Jaina's coat on the grain, Sylvanas's hands in the loft. Jaina backs Sylvanas against Havel before being asked (stands at her shoulder, sets the staff down) and offers the jaw plan; Sylvanas had been about to ask. Reliance is plain and unspoken: Sylvanas thinks 'Jaina' and worries she will be 'white by the time the bell went'; aloud she says 'Proudmoore'. No warmth language; harder to pull apart, not softer.
currentState_chapter6: Chapter 6 (Jaina's POV): two women reading the same failure. Sylvanas tests Jaina's plain statement ('Somebody.') and presses on how she will show it to a man who cannot feel it; at Strahnbrad she reads the camp faster than Jaina, hands her the evidence, stays behind her, and calls Arthas's decision to his face before Jaina finishes. Jaina, who hoped proof would show her too cynical about a prince she never met, says aloud 'You were right. At the fork.' Sylvanas gives the verdict ('a good commander, with an enemy he can see... He'll fight that war... The other one is ours.') and asks nothing about the history; Jaina offers nothing. They turn the horses to Andorhal together. On the road Sylvanas asks Jaina to read the tally-man (a legitimate use of Jaina's sense); Jaina answers honestly, 'Nothing but a tired clerk', and Sylvanas accepts it and says only 'Twice, it's wrong.' Jaina thinks the turn in the saddle out of proportion; she does not know Sylvanas has been turning the carter over since Ch5. At the crest Sylvanas waits for Jaina's word ('Sylvanas turned to her and waited.') and follows it ('The market gate.'). No thanks, no warmth spoken. Aloud: Jaina 'Ranger-General', Sylvanas 'Mage' (or 'Proudmoore' before others).
currentState_chapter5: Chapter 5: a working pair with a clean split of labour and a working trust that is spent in acts, not words. Jaina reads roads; Sylvanas reads paper and ground; the sheet they draw together is two maps that confirm each other. Jaina gives one-word reads, moves her marks without pride and does not lecture; Sylvanas waits for the lecture and does not get it. At the fork Sylvanas uses the read to choose the road ('How sure?' 'As sure as Brent's.'), cannot verify it, and refuses a re-read ('No.'). Her interior name for Jaina shifts to 'Jaina' (first time ever, interior only): 'Jaina, then.' Aloud she still says 'Mage' and, as a work command, 'Proudmoore' ('Proudmoore. Read him.', 'Proudmoore. Barov.'). Jaina still says 'Ranger-General'. The one admitted dependency: 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.' Still no praise, no thanks, no warmth spoken.
currentState_chapter4: A working pair with its first shared win, and still tense. Jaina has seen Sylvanas's method (people, fear, supply, authority) work on Brask, and has asked herself whether it can be learned; she relapses once ('maps') and by dusk brings the human side of the problem straight to her in the real register ('Well, mage?' answered in full). Sylvanas's trust is shown by acts only: 'Let my mage see your sick', 'Can you leave them?', 'Mage. Will it hold?', accepting Jaina's night-shutdown warning and putting it to Brask in her own low voice. Jaina's narration changes from 'Windrunner' to 'Sylvanas' mid-chapter; aloud still 'Ranger-General'. Sylvanas still only 'Mage'. No open trust, no warmth, no thanks beyond 'Thank you, Ranger-General.'
currentState_chapter3: Custodian and prisoner turned into a working pair that is not allowed to say so. Sylvanas still thinks of her as 'the mage' (never 'Jaina') and 'the prisoner' when she is thinking about custody, still gives the orders about where and when and what ('Houses first', 'You're done reading with those tonight'), but has stopped treating the mage's read as optional: waits for it, takes 'I don't know' as a straight answer, lets her refusal to call the storehouse the source stand, hands her the ground she cannot read (the prints, the cut), and rides south on it while telling herself it is 'the trail'. No warmth. Jaina is formal ('Ranger-General') and unembarrassed about saying no or 'I don't know'.
powerDynamic: Sylvanas controls movement, ground, sequence and terms (houses before ground, the well chosen and covered, hands banned for the night, the order of march 'Mage, in the middle'). Jaina controls what the contamination is and where it is heavy; she wins arguments by method ('a store is where things end up') and is believed by action, not praise. Sylvanas cannot perceive any of the read herself (staff in her fist is 'a stick, and cold'; her hand finds nothing), so she must trust it spoken aloud. Jaina is still custody: told to keep her lid on her ink, to ride in the middle, to stay at the door.
powerDynamic_chapter7: Sylvanas still gives the orders, the route and the rendezvous ('Back here. When the Exchange rings the night shift.'), and divides the work by skill: Jaina holds the sample room and the read of the grain; Sylvanas holds the men. Jaina does not argue the split. The new inversion: Jaina is the one who makes a plan Sylvanas needs (the jaw), offers it unasked, and sets the terms of her own cost ('I can only do it once tonight'); Sylvanas accepts without comment.

nameUsage_chapter7.sylvanasCallsJaina: Aloud 'Proudmoore' in front of the others ('Proudmoore. The sample room. Take him.'); no 'Mage' this chapter. Interior: 'Jaina' (one 'the mage' in passing).
nameUsage_chapter7.jainaCallsSylvanas: Aloud 'Ranger-General' ('Every bag on one of Corin's copied marks is bad, Ranger-General'; 'My escort.' of her to the gate clerk).

trajectory_chapter7: Chapter 7: practical trust -> a working dependency Sylvanas does not name. The raid exists only because both halves exist. She thinks 'Jaina' and worries; Jaina steps up before being asked; neither says it.
powerDynamic_chapter6: Sylvanas still sets pace and route and the shape of the conversation ('Make it short'); at the crest she turns and waits for Jaina to name the destination, and Jaina does ('The market gate'). Jaina is now openly the instrument and the case-maker; Sylvanas is the reader of men and camps. The dependence is mutual: the paper moves from Sylvanas's coat to Jaina's fingers and back; Sylvanas asks Jaina what she read; Jaina concedes the read of Arthas. Neither defers in tone.

nameUsage_chapter6.sylvanasCallsJaina: Aloud: 'Mage' alone or in company of the party ('He has orcs in his hills, Mage. Make it short.', 'Give it here, Mage.', 'Mage. Did you read anything off him?'); 'Proudmoore' before outsiders (to the sergeant; behind Jaina in front of Arthas). Never 'Jaina' aloud. (Interior not shown in Ch6.)

powerDynamic_chapter5: Sylvanas commands sequence, route and risk (the table, the night ride, the fork, 'No.'); Jaina is the sole instrument for the unseen layer. Sylvanas cannot check Jaina's marks except against paper, and 'so far, every mark she could lay against a book had matched it'; for the south-road call there is no paper, only trust. Jaina concedes the hierarchy ('Count them, then... I'd rather you counted them than took my word'), sits when she needs to, and accepts the delegated job: 'Then I'll have to show it to them.' Sylvanas cannot see the read either; the dependence is shared.
powerDynamic_chapter4: Sylvanas still commands where and when ('Mage. What you find, I want before dark.', 'Then we're quick.', 'Lyriel. With the mage.'); she asks rather than orders on the matters only Jaina can answer ('How sure?', 'Can you leave them?', 'Will it hold?') and accepts the answers. Jaina wins on tempo (the baker lights his oven before light) by talking to Sylvanas, not Brask. Jaina refuses to stay by the water butt by lifting her staff and Sylvanas lets her follow ('There, then.'). Each has a domain: Jaina the body and the spell, Sylvanas the village, supply and authority.

physicalDynamics.pattern: Sylvanas stands close enough that the seated mage must tip her head back; Jaina reads Sylvanas head to toe and her face last, then holds her gaze.
In the cell: Sylvanas watches Jaina's mouth, not her eyes; steps in half a pace and sets a hand flat on the wall a hand's breadth from Jaina's head ('Which stones read worst. Where.').
On the road Sylvanas rides ahead with her back to Jaina and does not turn her head; Jaina rides at her off-side quarter a length behind to talk. Jaina's hand gestures stop mid-air when corrected.
When Jaina goes under at the culvert Sylvanas stands over her with bow and an arrow on the string, the point to the ground; calls her three times.
Sylvanas kneels across the doe from Jaina in the ditch water with the knife over her knee, waiting.

Chapter 3: Sylvanas keeps the mage at doors 'where I can see your hands'; Jaina starts to draw a figure in the air and stops at 'Houses first'; Sylvanas hauls the well bucket for her ('Water first. Would you?'), stands with her back to the well-head while Jaina kneels with the staff across her thighs, and goes down on one knee to take her wrist and pull her hand off the frozen stones; later holds out her hand on the cellar ladder ('Give it here') and takes the staff for a moment; stands in a doorway to cover her; hands the staff down into the hole; 'Sylvanas turned away' when Neral comforts the girl while Jaina sits against the wall; lets her sleep on the ride and lets her wake in her own time at the noon water; at the table Jaina opens the ink tin with her teeth and sets it by Sylvanas's elbow.

Chapter 4: Sylvanas hands her bow up to Cyndia and walks forward unarmed; Jaina watches with her hands closed on the reins ('stopped breathing somewhere around the cradle'); at the chapel Sylvanas stops at the end of Elsie's door-bed, back to the wall, and reads the room; Jaina looks at the grey glove and chooses the real register; at the granary corner Sylvanas points at the ground ('There. Stay.') and Jaina lifts the staff an inch; Sylvanas's mouth goes thin, then she points behind her heels ('There, then.'); in the loft Sylvanas is across the room before Jaina sees her cross it, and Jaina's frost pins the boy while Sylvanas has both hands full of lamp; at the cage Jaina comes up beside Sylvanas at the bars and then kneels at Tam's body while Sylvanas holds his mouth; Jaina speaks to her low, 'as Sylvanas had spoken to him at the spear'; late night Sylvanas on the threshold, 'Thank you, Ranger-General.'; at dawn she shows Jaina the ANDORHAL sacking and 'Mage. Up.' Jaina mounts and sits shaking; Sylvanas turns the mare onto the grain road without a word.

Chapter 5: Sylvanas takes the mage's reins at crossings and watches her face; asks 'Can you read from the crossing?'; has a hand ready for the mage's elbow and does not need it; pinches the candle out so Jaina's hair is safe; Jaina leans in at the bench to put a dry fingertip beside Ashford; shares a pen, a sheet and the stub of lead; Sylvanas reads, Jaina marks; at the fork Jaina sits on the floor without being told and picks frost off her finger.

Chapter 6: Sylvanas turns in the saddle to hear the plain line and looks Jaina over once, crystal, hand on the reins, before returning to her face; faces forward while she says 'Paper. He'll have clerks for paper.'; gets down at the hedge, holds the sheet up to Jaina's stirrup, passes the mare's rein to Cyndia and steps back; stands behind Jaina during the audience and speaks past her shoulder; steps into the space Arthas left, holds out her hand ('Give it here, Mage.'), pushes the slips back in, folds the sheet small and takes it back into her coat when Jaina's fingers fail; gives a short nod to 'Andorhal.'; puts her horse across the tally-man's path; turns round in the saddle at the farewell and asks Jaina to read; waits for Jaina at the crest.

Chapter 7: at the gate, Jaina stands at Sylvanas's right with the pass held in two bare fingertips; the clerk starts to ask about 'Windrunner' and Jaina cuts him off ('My escort.'). At the bench Jaina stays on her feet with the staff under her dead arm; Sylvanas looks at her and decides. At the table Jaina rises, comes round the end of it and sets the staff down at Sylvanas's shoulder, facing Havel across it. Sylvanas turns her sheet round to face Jaina and mimes the glove. Sylvanas had been about to ask when Jaina offered.

nameUsage_chapter5.sylvanasCallsJaina: Aloud: 'Mage.' (twice at the first depot), 'Proudmoore. Read him.', 'Proudmoore. Barov.', 'Mage, with me.' Never 'Jaina' aloud. Interior narration: 'the mage' until the fork scene; there, 'Jaina had been on her feet before the question was cold. Jaina, then.' From then on, in interior narration, 'Jaina' (Sylvanas's first use of the name even in thought, tied to 'Jaina' in Lyriel's mouth: 'That man was paid by the loop, Jaina.').

nameUsage_chapter4.sylvanasCallsJaina: 'Mage' aloud every time; 'my mage' to Brask; never 'Jaina' or 'Proudmoore'.
nameUsage_chapter4.jainaCallsSylvanas: Aloud 'Ranger-General' (incl. the low ask at the cage). Narration: 'Windrunner' until the chapel-window scene; 'Sylvanas' thereafter (and in thought: 'Sylvanas Windrunner' once, in the Millhaven-storehouse memory). A small hinge: the interior name shifts first.

nameUsage.sylvanasCallsJaina: 'Mage' in direct address ('Mage. With me.', 'Mage. Up.'); 'Proudmoore' twice at the well when the mage will not come up ('Proudmoore.', '*Proudmoore!*'); 'the mage' in narration and thought throughout chapter 3; 'the prisoner' in custody thoughts. Never 'Jaina'.
nameUsage.jainaCallsSylvanas: 'Ranger-General' every time aloud, even when pushing back or apologising ('Ranger-General, it's right under us.', 'Ranger-General, a store is where things end up.'). In her Ch2 narration 'Windrunner', 'the Ranger-General', once 'the elf', 'this soldier'.

history.event: Sylvanas read Jaina's Farstrider file last winter and wrote her off as a future nuisance, 'gifted beyond her years'.
Sylvanas touched a wrong stone at noon; the same stone is circled on Jaina's map. Jaina does not know this.
First face-to-face in the cell; Sylvanas opens with 'Start talking.'
Jaina gives her first account (short version), admits nobody sent her; Sylvanas asks 'Why alone?'; Sylvanas lists terms; Jaina accepts them.
Sylvanas refuses Jaina's request to stop on the hill ('Not on the hill'), then grants it at the culvert.

Jaina tries the river-over-banks explanation; Sylvanas cuts in with 'Your lines don't spread' and the ruled-line closure at Millhaven. Jaina is humiliated, then speaks to her as to Antonidas (source or sink). Sylvanas answers 'How much deeper?... Then I pick the ground.'
In the ambush Jaina hears Sylvanas's commands and can 'draw the whole fight from those calls'; Sylvanas orders her into the ditch to read the doe and opens it with her own knife.
At the Millhaven crossing Jaina asks to read at once; Sylvanas refuses ('Houses first'), sweeps, then picks the ground and covers her; Sylvanas's 'Then I pick the ground' from Ch2 is paid off.
At the well Jaina fails to come up; Sylvanas drags her out by the wrist. Jaina's honest report: 'I don't know... I'm sorry.' Sylvanas thinks 'It was a straight answer, at least.'

Storehouse: Jaina refuses to call the loudest place the source. Sylvanas had expected her to grab it (a magister would have signed it); she does not argue ('Damn her, then. The hand.'), and orders her to stop reading with her hands that night.

In the lane Sylvanas asks the mage whether she can hear anything in the prints without her hands; Jaina's read ('It's in the prints... heavier where they stepped') is received as fact. They exchange 'They walked out.' / 'Which way?'
The mage pays the Ch2 promise to check the horses (clean); Sylvanas says 'Then look.' and 'Wrap the mage's hands.' (Cyndia carries it out).

In the cut Sylvanas asks 'Mage. Can you tell her which marks are which?'; Jaina's heavy/light sorting gives Cyndia the count; Jaina notes the dead did not use their road ('They didn't go up our road. Did they?' 'No.').

Dispatch: Jaina brings the ink and pen; Sylvanas: 'They know it already. It's in your file.' Jaina's ears redden. Sylvanas keeps the mage rather than sending her north: 'you did not hand a Kirin Tor apprentice to a relay rider with a child on her saddle.'
On the ride south Sylvanas lets the mage sleep; at noon the mage reports 'wider... ahead of us... down the road.' Sylvanas to herself: 'No. On the trail. The read was the trail.'
Chapter 4 entry: Jaina has rested and arrives cheerful; she sees the sickness spread thin; Sylvanas stops the line at Brask's spear.

In the lane Sylvanas defuses Brask in a low voice, hands off her bow, tells him Millhaven in objects, and offers 'let my mage see your sick, and we'll know by dark whether I'm a liar'. Jaina thinks she was wrong about Windrunner ('maps'), asks 'Could it be learned?'.

Sylvanas goes to the granary by her own road (supply) while Jaina reads the sick; at the window Jaina watches her and is annoyed, 'unable to decide whether it was with Sylvanas for getting there or with herself for being surprised'; she is in fact thinking 'Sylvanas' now.
Dusk report: Jaina gives the gut-bread analysis in full; Cyndia gives the supplier; both converge on 'Somebody is selling it to them on--' 'On purpose.'
Granary: Sylvanas leaves Jaina by the water butt; Jaina lifts the staff; in the loft their two methods work in sequence: arrow, frost, shell, read.

Cage: Tam dies; Sylvanas and Jaina each carry a different part (Sylvanas the fingers and the collar; Jaina the gut-read: clean). Jaina chooses not to explain the stack to Brask but to ask Sylvanas for the night shutdown; Sylvanas gives Brask the deadline 'until cockcrow' in her spear-lane voice.

Dawn: Sylvanas shows Jaina the ANDORHAL sacking; Jaina doubts it ('Or where he wanted us to think it came from'); Sylvanas folds it into her coat ('Either way, it's the road he drove.'); they ride on south-west together.

Chapter 5: at Corley's yard Sylvanas sends the mage to the crossing; Jaina reads four roads; they draw two pictures on one sheet that do not sit together at first (north oldest, east light), then agree against the book's counts; the mage's marks match Cyndia's counts and dates ('So far, every mark she could lay against a book had matched it'). Sylvanas expects a lecture and gets one-word reads.
Chapter 5: Jaina bars and moves her own mark at Hollow Green after Cyndia's list; Sylvanas notes that a Silvermoon magister would let a village burn before moving a mark of his own.

Chapter 5: on the overseer, Sylvanas orders 'Proudmoore. Read him.'; Jaina: 'Nothing on him, Ranger-General. No more than on you.' Sylvanas lets the overseer go on a warm room's word. Later she carries the error alone; Jaina does not remark on it. The mage looks at her once in the last light before turning the mare back.
Chapter 5: at the river depot ash, Sylvanas: 'Proudmoore. Barov.' Jaina supplies the Barov house and granaries. 'There's nothing in them... It's only paper.'

Chapter 5 fork: they read the slips; Jaina's reads cluster on the south road; she stands on the doorstone and the staff light leans toward the bend (teeth chattering, frost). 'That's enough.' Sylvanas thinks 'Jaina, then.' Sylvanas pins Strahnbrad with her knife; Jaina offers a re-read from the first bridge; Sylvanas: 'No.' 'Expect them to get in the way.' 'Then I'll have to show it to them.' 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.'

Chapter 6: on the climb Jaina says 'It's one thing... It comes in on the wagons and walks out on its own feet.' Sylvanas: 'Somebody.' Jaina: 'Somebody with training... I can't tell you who, or how...' Sylvanas: 'And when you say that to a man who can't feel any of it?' Jaina: slips, sacking, the map with the knife hole; 'Paper. He'll have clerks for paper.' 'Then he can come with me to a granary and watch.' 'He has orcs in his hills, Mage. Make it short.'

Chapter 6: Sylvanas reads the camp and its blind side (east pickets, one sergeant and a hedge); Jaina follows her look 'and was slower'; Jaina privately expects Arthas to prove Sylvanas too hard on a prince she never met.

Chapter 6: at the audience Jaina presses for men to shut the Andorhal granaries; Sylvanas says behind her 'He's going to write to his father, Proudmoore, and then he's going back up that hill.' Arthas confirms ('Yes. I am.'). After he leaves, Jaina tells Sylvanas 'You were right. At the fork... And you called it in front of him before I'd finished.' Sylvanas gives the verdict on Arthas. 'And the other one?' 'Is ours.' Jaina waits for Sylvanas to ask about the history and she does not; Jaina does not offer it.

Chapter 6: Sylvanas asks 'Did you read anything off him?' of the tally-man; Jaina: 'Nothing but a tired clerk.' 'Why? What was it?' 'The blessing. I had the same one at Millhaven...' 'It's a farewell. Country people have dozens of them.' 'Once, it's a farewell. Twice, it's wrong.' Jaina does not recall the Millhaven wagon's words.
Chapter 7: Sylvanas writes the cover pass under her own seal; Jaina answers the gate clerk flat and cuts off the question about the Ranger-General.

Chapter 7: at the bench, Sylvanas sends Jaina with Corin and Lyriel to the sample room and takes the district herself; Jaina names the limits ('I won't know who put it there'), Sylvanas: 'That's mine.' Sylvanas privately recalls it had been easier at Corley's with a shout between them.

Chapter 7: the halves fit at once at the post (Jaina: the coat on the grain, bags heavy/clean; Sylvanas: the eight, the runner, the five masked at Kett's). Sylvanas lays her sketch beside Corin's column and says 'I have the hands.' Jaina: 'Necromancy. Both.'

Chapter 7: Jaina asks Havel what is left in the loft, steps up beside Sylvanas before being asked, says the loft is wet tonight, and offers to freeze one man's jaw before he can bite; Sylvanas had been about to ask. Sylvanas assigns Cyndia and Lyriel around the pair.

trajectory_chapter6: Chapter 6: the fight over whether Lordaeron will listen is over; the old prejudice has less room to hide (Jaina concedes Sylvanas read Arthas and the army better; Sylvanas treats Jaina's sense as a tool worth asking). Anger now points outward. Still no thanks, warmth or first-name use aloud. Next: Havel at the market gate; Jaina's body is failing (nosebleed, frost) and Sylvanas has not remarked on it on page. The tally-man's farewell is Sylvanas's private mark that Jaina half-dismisses.
trajectory: Chapter 5: practical trust, clean division of labour, a first admission of dependence ('I can't see it either'), and Sylvanas's interior switch from 'the mage' to 'Jaina'. Next: the army on the south road will be the first test of Jaina showing the thing to others; Sylvanas will still say 'Mage' aloud. Warmth must stay unspoken (plan: no sudden warmth).
trajectory_chapter4: Chapter 4: grudging working pair -> first clean win together (the village lives). Jaina begins to treat Sylvanas as someone who solves the human side; Sylvanas treats Jaina's answers as actionable on the spot. Still tense, no trust spoken, no 'Jaina' from Sylvanas (plan: not earned before later chapters). Next: Andorhal, three days by cart.
trajectory_chapter3: Custody -> grudging working pair. Sylvanas 'stops treating the mage's read as optional' but does not trust her or name her; she stays 'the mage' in narration. Jaina's method (refusing the loud answer, saying 'I don't know') is what earns this. Next: the south, where Sylvanas must follow the mage's staff into a village that is alive and misreading itself; expect the 'trail, not the mage' self-deception to be tested.
